study type: secondary analysis of a multicenter cohort study
exposure: isolated severe systolic hypertension (systolic blood pressure >=160 mmHg with diastolic pressure <110 mmHg)
mild hypertension (systolic blood pressure 140-159 mmHg and/or diastolic blood pressure 90-109 mmHg)
outcome: composite of adverse maternal outcomes (hypertensive stroke, pulmonary edema, elevated creatinine, disseminated intravascular coagulation, cardiopulmonary arrest, death)
cohort: The cohort comprised 115,502 patients admitted for delivery between 2008 and 2011 across 25 hospitals, who had systolic blood pressure >=140 mmHg and/or diastolic blood pressure between 90 and 109 mmHg during their admission.
finding: Severe hypertension defined solely by systolic blood pressure (diastolic <110 mmHg) showed a stepwise association with a composite of adverse maternal outcomes, primarily driven by pulmonary edema and elevated creatinine, when compared to mild hypertension.
followup_time: Until maternal hospital discharge following delivery
